headline: Highest risk is data leakage: Chatwoot handles customer data and broad egress, while awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and has no shared channel, so other interaction risks stay low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default channel is documented between awesome-selfhosted and Chatwoot. awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, while Chatwoot’s documented APIs are integrations, not a bridge to the list. Without a shared channel, prompt injection is not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the pair, reassess injection risk.
IF Chatwoot begins ingesting awesome-selfhosted content as instructions, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Do not pipe list content into Chatwoot prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, and it has broad network egress. awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge-management list with no runnable surface, so it is not itself a leak source; the pair risk comes from Chatwoot exporting sensitive data to external services through its integrations.
conditions: IF Chatwoot integrations send customer records to third-party services, leakage risk is active.
IF the pair is deployed on a shared workspace with exported customer artifacts, exposure increases.
mitigations: Review outbound destinations for Slack, Dialogflow, Shopify, Google Translate, and Linear.
Restrict customer-data exports to approved accounts.
requires-engineering: add DLP or egress allowlisting.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and requests no permissions, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. Chatwoot exposes integrations but no overlapping filesystem, git, or OAuth write scopes are documented here. With no shared write surface, capability conflict is not evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or repository, reassess conflict.
IF shared OAuth scopes are configured for a mutable resource, conflict risk changes.
mitigations: Avoid mounting a shared writable workspace.
Review Chatwoot integration scopes before enabling them.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-selfhosted can be used as a reference source, but it is not runnable and does not produce authoritative actions. Chatwoot has action-capable integrations, yet no documented pipeline shows it consuming awesome-selfhosted output by default. The cascade is therefore possible only through manual operator chaining.
conditions: IF an operator copies list-derived recommendations into Chatwoot actions without verification, cascade risk appears.
IF Chatwoot automation is configured to trust external text as facts, severity increases.
mitigations: Require human review before any Chatwoot action.
Do not treat awesome-selfhosted entries as verified operational facts.
Use a checklist for any copied recommendations.
requires-engineering: add validation before automated actions.

E_compliance.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a public open-source knowledge list with no touched data classes, while Chatwoot handles customer data and messages. No residency, retention, or certification mismatch is documented between them, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary handling of Chatwoot’s customer data rather than a pair-specific violation.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is routed into a jurisdictionally restricted service, compliance risk increases.
IF retention policies differ across Chatwoot integrations, reassess.
mitigations: requires-engineering: map residency and DPA obligations per connector.
